name: s3-multipart
facts: A successful multipart upload requires initiation, each part and completion; part retransmission adds requests.
Unfinished multipart parts remain stored until completed or explicitly aborted. Multipart listing and copies need separate inventory.

name: s3-multipart-limits
facts: Use a conditional64MiB part size and count ceil(bytes/partsize); actual transfer-client configuration remains unimplemented.

name: s3-kms
facts: SSE-KMS uploads require GenerateDataKey, downloads require Decrypt and multipart requires both permissions.
The one-KMS-per-S3-operation proposal is a modeling envelope, not a documented universal hard operation maximum. Do not deduct bucket-key/cache benefits.

name: emr-certificates
facts: EMR4.8.0–7.10.0 supports PEMzip or a custom certificate provider, while EMR-managed certificates begin7.11.0.

A PEMzip requires privateKey.pem and certificateChain.pem; trust and hostnames need explicit handling. The AWS self-signed example is a proof-of-concept, not production approval. No key is generated/read here.

name: emr-storage
facts: The default xlarge table lists two32GiB additional data volumes per EBS-only instance.
Require explicit one32GiB gp3 data disk plus explicit32GiB gp3 root on each of the two nodes, and verify four total volumes in plan/inventory.

name: iam-simulator
facts: AWS policy simulation does not make the simulated service request and has documented differences from actual service behavior.
Local mocks/policy tests do not prove actual EMR tagging or consistency; any later simulator API call remains separately gated account access.

name: spark-yarn-v3.5.4
facts: With-Hadoop Spark normally omits the cluster Hadoop classpath; explicitly keep populateHadoopClasspath=false for the isolated runtime.
If neither yarn.archive nor yarn.jars is set Spark can build/upload a JAR zip for distributed cache. Count any separate S3 staging object; do not assume it costs no bytes or requests.

name: spark-security-v3.5.4
facts: Spark authentication and RPC encryption are not automatic. The pinned security document describes authEngineVersion2 and authenticated AES/GCM mode.
Local spill encryption does not protect every application output file; EMR configuration and POSIX filesystem protections remain separate requirements.
